Automated Model Briefing

⚠ AI-generated text — may be wrong, incomplete, or overconfident. This is automated commentary on experimental model output, not flight advice and not a weather forecast. It has not been reviewed by a meteorologist.

Overall Assessment Moderate thermal day with peak lift around 300–365 ft/min at most sites. Light winds allow comfortable soaring at many locations, but a persistent easterly crosswind renders Hallelujah and Daydreams unfavorable. Low-level shear and isolated cloud overdevelopment require caution at a few sites.

Site Breakdown

  • Kingsbury grade: Favorable — light thermals and minimal wind. Preferred window 10am–3pm, peak w* 307 ft/min, thermal ceiling 1580 ft AGL.
  • Hallelujah: Unfavorable — strong crosswind (25–26 mph from ~105°) opposite launch direction, plus hazardous low-level shear (8 mph/layer). Not flyable today.
  • Slide Mountain: Favorable — well-aligned light wind and consistent thermals. Window 8am–3pm, peak w* 275 ft/min, thermal ceiling 1076 ft AGL.
  • McClellan: Favorable — good thermals with light, mostly acceptable wind. Window 9am–5pm, peak w* 347 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2146 ft AGL.
  • West McClellan: Marginal — off-direction wind precludes ridge soaring; sled runs possible in light wind. Window 10am–4pm, peak w* 290 ft/min, thermal ceiling 1833 ft AGL.
  • Peavine Mountain: Marginal — weak thermals (peak 234 ft/min) and 14% cloud cover/overdevelopment limit soaring. Brief window 10am–3pm, thermal ceiling only 624 ft AGL.
  • Rainbow Ridge: Favorable with caution — well-aligned wind and strong thermals, but low-level shear (5 mph/layer) is marginal. Window 9am–5pm, peak w* 364 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2438 ft AGL.
  • Duck Hill: Marginal — wind direction off for ridge soaring; usable for thermal/sled flights. Window 9am–5pm, peak w* 323 ft/min, thermal ceiling 2221 ft AGL.
  • Daydreams: Unfavorable — strong crosswind (22–23 mph from ~95–100°) and 23% overdevelopment risk. Not recommended.

Hazards

  • Low-level shear — Hazardous layer speed shear at Hallelujah (8 mph/583 ft AGL) and marginal at Rainbow Ridge (5 mph/405 ft AGL).
  • Rotor/lee turbulence — Easterly flow may create lee turbulence downwind of Peavine Mountain and the Carson Range, especially strong at Hallelujah and Daydreams.
  • Overdevelopment — Elevated risk of cloud build-up inside the thermal zone at Daydreams (23% of flying hours) and Peavine (14%); may cause shading, gust fronts, and suppressed lift.

Site Forecast ?Top of Thermals (PBLH) — height of the turbulent mixing layer; thermals typically reach this ceiling.
LCL (Lifted Condensation Level) — altitude where rising air reaches its dew point; theoretical cloud base.
Cloud Base — lowest model level with >10% cloud fraction.
w* — convective velocity scale; higher = stronger thermals (ft/min).
Cloud Cover — max cloud fraction over the column (0–100%).
Wind thresholds: orange = 12 mph, red = 18 mph.
